title: hosted-api cascade suppression and tenant fallthrough audit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several high-severity customer escalations in the last 48 hours were traced to a compound failure mode in the Hosted API: tenant surge -> proxy fanout amplification -> connection pool exhaustion -> KV cache compaction -> increased p99 latency -> aggressive client retries. The combination produced repeated 5xx/timeouts for some tenants and noisy retries that amplified the outage.

Root cause hypothesis: Two concurrent issues surfaced: (1) The proxy's async fallback path did not honor the tenant-scoped admission token, allowing certain requests to bypass per-tenant shaping and hit backend workers directly, causing localized overload. (2) The retry coordination logic in the gateway SDK used optimistic retries without sufficient jitter or idempotency checks for multipart/streaming requests, which increased simultaneous inflight requests and triggered KV cache compaction under memory pressure.

Observed impact: Several customers reported sustained 5xx and long tail timeouts for batch and streaming endpoints. Incident timelines show initial latency growth at 03:12 UTC, first customer escalation at 03:27 UTC, and sustained elevated error rates until partial mitigation deployed at 06:05 UTC. The Canary rollback for one patch occurred at 07:30 UTC due to unexpected client-side duplicate deliveries.

Proposed fixes and mitigations (short-term):
- Emergency config: enable tenant admission token enforcement in proxy to force per-tenant shaping (toggle: PROXY_TENANT_SHAPE=true).
- Fast-fail threshold: add server-side fast-fail for queue depth > 400ms tail to prevent long-lived head-of-line blocking.
- SDK safety: ship conservative retry policy update to SDKs (default max_retries=2, backoff with full jitter, idempotency header required for non-idempotent calls).
- Observability: add a tenant-level tracing tag propagation patch so we can attribute retries to originating request for correlation in traces.

Longer-term remediation (next 2 sprints):
- Tenant-scoped token-bucket admission controller with burst credits and hysteresis to avoid cold-start surges.
- KV-cache admission-time compaction changes to prefer prefix-preserving eviction under pressure rather than LRU-only compaction.
- Routing fallback: introduce a graceful degrade path that serves smaller model variants for overloaded tenants instead of synchronous retries.

Rollout plan:
1) Land proxy toggle and SDK conservative retries in a behind-feature-flag canary (5% traffic) with a 2-hour observation window.
2) If stable, expand to 25% then 50% over 8 hours, monitoring p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, and per-tenant error growth.
3) Release admission controller and KV cache changes in runtime-1.22 feature branch; full rollout gated on end-to-end canary and customer acceptance tests.

Monitoring / dashboards:
- Dashboards to watch: hosted-api/requests-by-tenant, hosted-api/5xx-by-path, kv-cache/eviction-rate, proxy/queue-depth, sdk/retry-rates-by-tenant.
- Alerts: page on sustained +50% p99 latency vs baseline for >10 minutes OR per-tenant 5xx rate >5% for >5 minutes.

Customer comms: Drafted outage summary for impacted customers (link below). Communication to customers will include immediate workaround (SDK upgrade to conservative retry policy), ETA for full fix, and offer for extended logs/export for affected customers.

Artifacts:
- RCA doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosts/reliability/ENG-101234-rca
- Patch PR (proxy toggle): https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/3248
- SDK PR (retry policy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2891
- Observability spec: https://docs.redwood.ai/observability/tenant-tracing-audit

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strict admission control reduces peak throughput for well-behaved heavy tenants; need product consent on rate ceilings.
- Conservative retries reduce individual customer latency but could increase tail for small requests; propose to make this opt-in per-team via account settings for early-adopters.

Definition of done:
- Emergency toggles deployed and validated in canary.
- SDK conservative retry release published and communicated.
- Tenant tracing propagation enabled and dashboarded.
- Post-deploy monitoring shows p99 latency and 5xx rates returned to baseline for impacted tenants.
- Postmortem completed and follow-ups created for long-term fixes.
